title: Geometry of the deformation
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), in the situation of
[def-pur-dnc-section-family] with $g:V\to B$ smooth of pure
relative dimension $d$ and $N_s\to B$ the normal bundle of the
section:

1. *the fibers.* The fiber of $\widetilde g$ over $1$ is
$(g:V\to B,s)$ and the fiber over $0$ is the
$\pi_N:N_s\to B$ with its zero section; hence by the
base-change compatibility of [def-pur-co-smoothness]
(applied to the closed immersions $i_1,i_0$ of the two
sections of $\mathbf A^1_B$),
$$
\qquad i_1^*F\simeq C(g,s),\qquad
i_0^*F\simeq C(\pi_N,0_N).\qquad\text{(the two fibers)}
$$
1. *the coordinates.* Since $s$ is a section of a smooth
map, etale-locally there are coordinates $x_1,\dots,x_d$ on
$V$ over $B$ in which $s$ is given by $x_i=0$ (the
relative form of the local linearization of
[lem-pur-regular-immersion-linearization], via
[sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form]); on the DNC chart the
coordinates are $u_i=x_i/t$, so $\widetilde g$ is smooth of
pure relative dimension $d$.
1. *the punctured trivialization.* Over $\mathbf G_{m,B}$
the deformation space is canonically
$$
D_sV|_{\mathbf G_{m,B}}\simeq V\times_B\mathbf G_{m,B},
\qquad \widetilde s|_{\mathbf G_{m,B}}=s\times 1,
$$
so base change for the cohomologically smooth $\widetilde g$
gives the canonical isomorphism
$$
\kappa^\circ:j^*F\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;j^*a^*C(g,s),
\qquad a:\mathbf A^1_B\to B.
$$
1. *the standard pair.* For the standard pair
$(\mathbf A^d_B\to B,0)$, the deformation space is
$\mathbf A^d_{B}\times_B\mathbf A^1_B$ with $x_k=tu_k$, the
family object is the pullback $a^*\bigl(0^*\omega_{\mathbf A^d_B/B}\bigr)$, and $0^*\omega_{\mathbf A^d_B/B}=\Lambda(d)[2d]$ by the vector-bundle purity of
[cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity].
1. *base change.* The Rees-algebra description of the
deformation space for a closed section, the punctured
trivialization, and the family object commute with base change
in $B$.

proof.text: Work at the finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ specified for this part of [def-pur-conventions]. Fix $b\in B$. Apply [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] near $s(b)$, shrinking the affine base so its section lies in the chosen source neighbourhood. Translate the affine coordinates by their values along $s$; then the chart $e:U\to\mathbf A^r_W$ sends $s|_W$ to zero. The chart is smooth of relative dimension zero by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]; composing with the affine projection and using [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] shows that $r=d$, since the relative dimension at $s(b)$ is $d$. The chart is separated: its diagonal is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $U\to W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], $Z=U\times_{\mathbf A^d_W}W\to W$ is separated etale with section $s|_W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion] that section is open and closed in $Z$. Delete $Z\setminus s(W)$ from $U$. Thus the inverse image of zero is exactly $s(W)$ scheme-theoretically, and on affine subcharts the ideal is $I=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)R$ for an etale $C=A[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\to R$. This is relative linearization; the absolute regular-immersion lemma is not applied to a possibly singular base.

source.place: Item (2), relative coordinates; expanded using Stacks 054L (morphisms.tex, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space), 02GO and 024T (etale.tex, proposition-properties-sections).

proof.text: Use the actual affine charts $D=R[t,I/t]$ of [def-pur-dnc-section-family]. On each chart meeting the section, [lem-pur-dnc-etale-rees-chart] gives $D\cong R\otimes_{A[x]}A[t,u]$, $x_i=tu_i$, and its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$. An affine open disjoint from the section has $I=R$, hence $R[t,I/t]=R[t,t^{-1}]$; its projection is the base change of $g$ to $\mathbf G_{m,B}$, smooth of relative dimension $d$ by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. These opens cover $V$, so their inverse images cover the actual deformation scheme and prove clause (2). Smoothness here is checked on the displayed local smooth ring presentations, as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. In particular no isomorphism $D\cong A[t,u]$ is asserted for a general etale $R$.

source.place: Item (2), the Rees chart; correction of the unit proof Coordinates paragraph: an etale chart, not necessarily an isomorphism.

proof.text: Inverting $t$ in the subalgebra $D=R[t,I/t]\subseteq R[t,t^{-1}]$ gives exactly $R[t,t^{-1}]$: the inclusion gives one direction and $R,t,t^{-1}$ generate the other. Consequently its $t=1$ fibre is $R$, since $t$ is already a unit modulo $t-1$. For the zero fibre use [lem-pur-rees-associated-graded-chart]: $D/(t)\cong\operatorname{gr}_I R$, with $[a/t^m]\leftrightarrow[a]_m$. The normal cone is precisely the relative spectrum of this graded algebra [def-pur-normal-bundle]. On the section charts of step 1, reduction of $R\otimes_{A[x]}A[t,u]$ modulo $t$ gives $(R/I)[u]$, with $u_i$ the classes of $x_i$ in degree one. Thus the canonical symmetric-algebra comparison is locally a polynomial-algebra isomorphism and the normal cone is the rank-$d$ normal bundle. All the identifications agree on overlaps: the punctured map fixes $R$ and $t$ and the graded map sends every $a/t^m$ to $[a]_m$. Under the augmentation $r\mapsto\bar r$, $a/t^m\mapsto0$ for $m>0$, the section restricts to $s$ at one and to the graded augmentation zero section at zero. This proves the geometric fibre and punctured-trivialization assertions.

For a Cartesian square of a smooth separated pure-dimensional map $f:X\to Y$ and $v:Y'\to Y$, write $u:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, and suppose its sections obey $u s'=s v$. By [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], the canonical base-change map $Lu^*\omega_f\to\omega_{f'}$ is invertible. Its map is the adjunction transpose specified in condition (3) of [def-pur-co-smoothness], rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between the endpoints. Apply $Ls'^*$ and the composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] to obtain
$$Lv^*C(f,s)=Lv^*Ls^*\omega_f\simeq Ls'^*Lu^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}Ls'^*\omega_{f'}=C(f',s').$$
Here $C$ is the actual object of [def-pur-section-invariant]. Every map to which this is applied below is smooth separated of finite type over the finite-type schemes of the conventions; the theorem has exactly these domains. This supplies the cohomological-smoothness hypothesis that the definition alone would not prove.

source.place: Items (1), (3), (5), condition (3) of cohomological smoothness, with its hypothesis supplied by the theorem.

proof.text:
Apply step 4 to $\widetilde g$ along $i_1,i_0$, using its smoothness from step 2 and the fibre squares and section identifications of step 3. Since $F=C(\widetilde g,\widetilde s)$ [def-pur-dnc-section-family], this gives $Li_1^*F\simeq C(g,s)$ and $Li_0^*F\simeq C(\pi_N,0_N)$. For the punctured object, first apply that same square construction along $j:\mathbf G_{m,B}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^1_B$, obtaining $Lj^*F\simeq C(g\times_B\mathbf G_m,s\times1)$. Apply it again to $g$ along $a j:\mathbf G_{m,B}\to B$. The inverse of the second comparison followed after the first gives
$$\kappa^\circ:Lj^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}L(a j)^*C(g,s)\simeq Lj^*La^*C(g,s).$$
The last arrow is [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Thus both fibre comparisons and the punctured comparison use the specified base-change maps.

source.place: Items (1) and (3), the two fibre isomorphisms and the specified punctured isomorphism.

proof.text:
For $V=\mathbf A^d_B$ and its zero section, use [lem-pur-dnc-etale-rees-chart] with $R=C=A[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$. It gives the actual standard deformation algebra $A[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]$ with $x_i=tu_i$. The map $D_0\mathbf A^d_B	o\mathbf A^1_B$ and its section are consequently the base change of $(\mathbf A^d_B	o B,0)$ along $a$. Step 4 identifies its family object with $La^*C(p_d,0)$. Apply [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] to the trivial rank-$d$ bundle and the étale coefficient unit $A_B^{\mathrm{et}}$. That corollary is stated in the ordinary-étale realization: it gives $p_d^{	imes}A_B^{\mathrm{et}}\cong A^{\mathrm{et}}_{\mathbf A^d_B}(d)[2d]$ with the étale Tate line $\mu_{\ell^r}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A$. The item's $\omega_{p_d}$ is the pro-étale constructible exceptional image: by [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], on the étale-origin input $\Lambda_B=
u_B^*A_B^{\mathrm{et}}$ (the case $a=0$ of [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent]) its value is $
u_{\mathbf A^d_B}^*p_d^{	imes}A_B^{\mathrm{et}}$. Apply $
u^*_{\mathbf A^d_B}$ to the étale isomorphism and compose with the comparison $
u_T^*A_T^{\mathrm{et}}(d)\cong A^{\mathrm{pro}}_T(d)$ of [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent] for $T=\mathbf A^d_B$ (the shift commutes with the exact functor $
u^*$). This gives $\omega_{p_d}\cong\Lambda_{\mathbf A^d_B}(d)[2d]$ with the pro-étale twist of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Pull back along zero to obtain $C(p_d,0)\cong L0^*(\Lambda_{\mathbf A^d_B}(d))[2d]$. For the twist pullback, use [lem-pur-integral-twist-line-inverse-image](3) for the integral line and (1) for its completed ring. Reduce its semilinear isomorphism modulo $\varpi_E^n$ (tensor with $(A_{E,n})$) using the reduction identification of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free](3). The resulting finite line is exactly the line of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Its d-fold tensor power pulls back by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]; hence the pulled-back twist is $\Lambda_B(d)$. This proves clause (4), including $d=0$.

source.place: Item (4), the standard pair and vector-bundle purity.

proof.text:
Let $B'\to B$ be arbitrary within the scheme conventions. On affine base opens write it as $A\to A'$. For a section chart as in step 1 put $C'=A'[x]$, $R'=R\otimes_AA'$, and $I'=(x)R'$. Etale base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] allows [lem-pur-dnc-etale-rees-chart] over both bases. Its canonical tensor maps give
$$R[t,I/t]\otimes_AA'\cong(R\otimes_CA[t,u])\otimes_AA'\cong R'\otimes_{C'}A'[t,u]\cong R'[t,I'/t].$$
The middle isomorphism is the unique one fixing the two coefficient factors and $t,u$; its inverse fixes those same generators. The tensor pushout universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] verifies these maps and their inverse composites. Hence the resulting map is the canonical Rees comparison $r\otimes a'\mapsto ra'$, $(f/t)\otimes1\mapsto f'/t$, not an existence-only comparison. Away from $s(B)$, $I=R$ and the same formula is just the Laurent-polynomial base-change isomorphism, with inverse defined on $R',t,t^{-1}$. This argument imposes no flatness on $A\to A'$.

source.place: Item (5), arbitrary base change: explicit tensor calculation on section charts and on the complement.

proof.text: The local comparisons of step 7 agree on overlaps because all send each Rees generator $r,t,f/t$ to its functorial image. Apply the relative-Spec base-change theorem [lem-weil-pbc-relative-spec-base-change] to these isomorphisms of the chart algebras to identify $D_{s'}V'$ with $D_sV\times_{\mathbf A^1_B}\mathbf A^1_{B'}$. The augmentation maps commute on those same generators ($f/t$ maps to zero); thus the comparison preserves $\widetilde s$. Inverting $t$ and setting $t=1,0$ in the very same maps gives the punctured and fibre comparisons, so they commute with this base change, rather than only admitting unrelated isomorphisms. The degree-one and higher-degree maps at zero send $[f]_m$ to $[f']_m$; hence they also give the canonical base-change identification of the normal bundles. Restriction of these formulas to source open subcharts and to etale charts is the tensor formula of [lem-pur-dnc-etale-rees-chart]; this supplies etale localization as well.

source.place: Item (5), gluing the Rees comparisons and checking punctured and zero-section compatibility.

proof.text:
Write $a':\mathbf A^1_{B'}\to\mathbf A^1_B$ and $h:D_{s'}V'\to D_sV$ for step 8. Apply the canonical exceptional base change of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] to $\widetilde g$, and pull it back along $\widetilde s'$:
$$La'^*F\simeq L\widetilde s'^*Lh^*\omega_{\widetilde g}\xrightarrow{\sim}L\widetilde s'^*\omega_{\widetilde g'}=F'.$$
The first arrow uses the section equality and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. This proves the family-object part of clause (5). For successive changes of base, finite etale compact-support exchanges paste by [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]. The transport of [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] gives the same equation on etale-origin pro-etale objects: in the two successive conjugated maps the intermediate comparison isomorphisms cancel. Their exceptional mates then paste by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], because the exceptional comparison is precisely the counit transpose of the inverse compact-support exchange [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Pulling the pasted equality back along the sections gives the same comparison as the successive maps. Applying this to the squares with $i_0,i_1,j$ shows that the fibre and punctured object identifications above commute with base change. In the standard pair it is the same square for $p_d$. Clause (5) concerns the family object; the base-change behaviour of the twist identification of step 6 is not used here.

source.place: Item (5), family-object base change and compatibility of the specified comparisons.

tool_uses.why: Relative smooth local coordinates, used as a geometric tool; absolute regular-immersion linearization would require hypotheses on the base not present here.
Converts the etale chart to smooth relative dimension zero to identify its number of coordinates.
Generic relative dimension under composition and base change, including the punctured chart.
The affine projection has the stated relative dimension, so the normal-form chart has d coordinates.
Generic etale base change for the zero preimage and the section-coordinate algebra after arbitrary base change.
Removes the other components of the inverse image of zero; a generic section-of-etale-map fact.
Existing algebraic tool calculating the tensor-product Rees chart and its smooth projection; no new copy is made.
Existing algebraic zero-fibre calculation used for the canonical normal-cone identification.
Orientation-free smoothness theorem supplies the hypothesis of condition (3); the definition alone cannot supply it.
Canonical composition of pullbacks used to compute the actual section comparisons.
Inverse image of the actual integral twist line; reduction gives the finite twist.
Identifies the finite twist line with the reduction of the integral rank-one line.
Monoidal derived pullback transports the positive tensor powers defining the d-th twist.
Generic algebraic pushout used to verify the chart base-change maps and their inverses.
Generic relative-Spec construction transfers the canonical algebra comparison to schemes.
Generic adjunction calculus verifies that successive canonical family comparisons are compatible.
Horizontal pasting for the finite ordinary etale compact-support exchanges.
Specified transport of those exchanges to the witnessed pro-etale objects; intermediate comparison maps cancel in pasting.
